summary_paragraph: A woman with metastatic breast cancer and gastroparesis was admitted for abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. She developed acute hypoxia without clear pulmonary cause, leading to transfer to the ICU. Imaging and echocardiography revealed a patent foramen ovale with right-to-left shunting, contributing to hypoxemia. She underwent successful PFO closure, after which her oxygen requirements decreased significantly. Her gastroparesis symptoms were managed with medication adjustments, including a switch to Tigan for nausea. She was also found to have C. difficile colonization without active infection, which did not require treatment. She improved steadily, was weaned off oxygen, and discharged home on aspirin and clopidogrel post-procedure, with follow-up planned in cardiology and gastroenterology.
